small_guidance:
- Add autotune configs with larger `BLOCK_SP` (e.g., 128) and/or tile across the `pw` dimension differently; current POW=16 means BLOCK_SP=16 covers a full row. Consider tiling 2D (ph, pw) together to amortize weight loads.
- Hoist the weight load out of the spatial loop: each program reuses the same `w_vals` for every (n, pd, ph, pw) but currently loads weights once per program -- fine. But weights are tiny (3*16*27 floats); preload all weights into registers/shared at kernel start instead of per (kd,kh,kw) load inside the loop.
- Try `num_warps=8` for BLOCK_SP=16 with BLOCK_OC=16 to expose more ILP; current best may be undersubscribing the SM.
large_guidance:
- Restructure to tile over OC as well (split BLOCK_OC), launching a 2D grid `(N*POD*POH*POW_tiles, OC_tiles)` so multiple programs can share input loads across OC tiles while keeping register pressure low.
- Promote the inner `(ic, kd, kh, kw)` chain to a single GEMM-K loop after gathering an im2col-style input slice per pooled output; use `tl.dot` on a [BLOCK_SP, K] × [K, BLOCK_OC] tile (K = IC * KD * KH * KW = 81, pad to 128) to leverage tensor cores instead of scalar FMA broadcast.
- Use channels_last (NDHWC) layout for the input/output so the IC axis is contiguous, enabling vectorized loads across the GEMM-K dimension.
